claims.text: Temporal overlap of individual metal nucleation events is the key determinant of single-phase crystal-structure selection in noble-metal-based HEA nanoparticles.
Tuning precursor metal–ligand complexation strengths can equalize the reduction kinetics of the constituent metals.
Matched metal reduction rates cause the metal species to nucleate and grow concurrently.
Concurrent nucleation and growth promote homogeneous mixing into a single-phase solid solution.
Mismatched reduction rates cause sequential nucleation.
Sequential nucleation promotes elemental segregation and phase separation.
Selectively strengthening ligand interactions with more readily reduced metals will slow their reduction to match that of less noble metals.
Equalized reduction rates cause all constituent species to reach supersaturation simultaneously.
Simultaneous supersaturation yields co-nucleation and growth of a homogeneous single-phase FCC or HCP solid solution.
A species that reduces significantly earlier forms compositionally biased seeds.
Compositionally biased seeds drive core–shell or phase-segregated morphologies.
Untuned synthesis produces mixed-phase nanoparticles with frequent phase separation and elementally segregated domains.
The untuned baseline has a single-phase yield below 50%.
Ligand tuning will increase the single-phase fraction from below 50% to above 80%.
Ligand tuning will produce a more uniform elemental distribution.
Ligand tuning will produce a narrow particle-size distribution.
The proposed mechanism applies to equimolar noble-metal systems containing 5–8 elements.
The applicable process window is a 10–50 °C/s thermal ramp to 200–400 °C in inert gas, with 0.01–0.1 M total metal and a ligand-to-metal ratio of 0.5–2.
Outside the stated composition and processing ranges, kinetic or thermodynamic effects may override ligand-mediated control.
Failure to obtain at least a 20 percentage-point improvement in single-phase fraction, or failure to synchronize reduction kinetics, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state and task target require more than five elements, whereas the stated boundary includes five-element systems.

The claimed valid range requires a ligand-to-metal ratio of 0.5–2, but the proposed control is described as having no ligands, placing it outside the stated applicability window and weakening the matched comparison.
